newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Nov 20.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government plan to link all parts of Ivory Coast to national telephone network has reached 40 of planned 105 areas for a cost of more than four billion CFA francs, officials say - Wildlife school in central Ivorian town of Bouafle makes domestic rearing of agouti, a forest delicacy and rodent ressembling a large rat or small furry pig, a reality. Head of school says project is part of efforts to create jobs in the countryside for young Ivorians.
- Port Autonome d'Abidjan changes telephone number statement from Ivorian commercial capital's port says. New number from Monday was +225 23 80 00 (Tel) 23 80 80 (Fax)
- Seminar examines ways in which Ivory Coast's capital Yamoussoukro, inland birthplace of independence president Felix Houphouet-Boigny, can became a capital in full sense of word.

- Third in a series of advertising features on Ivorian rubber producing company Societe Africaine de Plantations d'Heveas (SAPH), in which Ivorian group OCTIDE of entrepreneur Francois Bakou hold 83 percent stake. Wednesday's feature, which like the others also appeared in Le Jour and government daily Fraternite Matin, says OCTIDE, which bought its stake from the state in 1994, has restored SAPH's competitivity.
- Ivorian national carrier Air Ivoire says in advertisement it will add Freetown leg to its flight from Abidjan to Ghana on Wednesday and Friday from December 4

- Lawyer for seven soldiers dismissed from army on charges of trying to destabilise institutions of the republic at time of Ivory Coast's turbulent October 1995 presidential election says tribunal hearing and dismissal procedure were flawed. Six of the seven were officers.
- Market for orange juice in Europe grows by five to six percent a year, experts say
